title: Capacity reuse and hotset coalescing roadmap
author: Nina Patel
body:
Overview

This page describes the 12‑month roadmap for reducing redundant GPU capacity usage by improving capacity reuse and implementing hotset coalescing across the LLM serving platform. The initiative combines scheduler changes, runtime cache-cohesion, operator tooling, and new dashboards/alerts so that platform operators can increase utilization without compromising tail latency or SLOs.

Why this matters

- Unit economics: preliminary sims show a potential 18–30% reduction in GPU token cost per month with conservative reuse assumptions.
- Tail latency & SLO stability: without careful coalescing, reuse can increase contention and tail latency; this roadmap emphasizes safe rollouts and observability.
- Operator overhead: better tooling reduces manual tenant eviction and ad‑hoc capacity reservations.

Scope and goals (12 months)

1) Technical goals (quantitative)
   - Achieve >= 20% capacity reuse rate for eligible bursts by Q4 2026.
   - Keep P99 tail latency impact <= +5% vs baseline during rollouts.
   - Reduce manual eviction incidents by 50% year-over-year.

2) Operational goals
   - Ship operator dashboards and a single runbook for hotset misbehavior.
   - Create a safe canary DSL and gating rules for all scheduler changes.

Milestones and timeline

- Q1 2026 — Research & prototypes
  - Dataset: collect 8 weeks of heatmap traces (tenant, model, seq_len histogram) from regional clusters.
  - Prototype two coalescing heuristics: affinity-based (warmset) and time-window coalescing.
  - Deliver: prototype report + simulation harness.

- Q2 2026 — Scheduler integration & operator tooling
  - Integrate warmset-aware placement into allocator v2.
  - Build operator UI: "Hotset Insights" panel with per-tenant hotness score and suggested coalescing groups.
  - Deliver: internal beta in staging region.

- Q3 2026 — Observability and safe rollout
  - Add dashboards and alerts (spec below).
  - Run progressive canaries: 5% -> 20% -> 50% of regional traffic with strict SLO gating.
  - Deliver: production toggle + documented rollback criteria.

- Q4 2026 — Optimization and expansion
  - Turn on cross-region coalescing in banded regions.
  - Evaluate cost savings and operational incidents; prepare postmortem/retrospective.

Architecture summary

- Components involved:
  - Allocator (allocator-v2): receives tenant burst hints and places into hotset shards.
  - Runtime prefix/KV cache controller: manages shared warmset caches across colocated workloads.
  - Operator UI & API: suggests groupings and allows manual opt-out.
  - Observability pipeline: heatmap aggregator -> hotset index -> dashboards.

- Decision heuristics (high level):
  - Hotness score = weighted function(model_qps, recent_seq_mean, prefix_reuse_ratio, rolling_error_rate).
  - Coalesce when score > threshold AND predicted P99 increase < 3% (simulator estimate).

Observability: dashboards and alerting (required spec)

Primary dashboards (tile list)
- Hotset Overview (per-region): capacity_reuse_rate, hotset_coalesced_tokens/s, coalesced_tenants_count, p50/p95/p99 latency by coalesced vs non-coalesced.
- Tenant Hotness Leaderboard: top 200 tenants by hotness score with annotations for model and plan.
- Coalescing Safety Monitor: real-time delta of P99, throttled_request_rate, evictions_triggered.

Alert rules (operator-critical)
- Alert: Hotset P99 regression
  - Query: region.coalesced_p99 / region.noncoalesced_p99 > 1.07 for 5m
  - Severity: P1 if affects >= 20% of capacity
  - Runbook: see "Hotset misbehavior runbook" (section below)

- Alert: Eviction storm
  - Query: evictions_count_rate > 50/min for 3m
  - Severity: P0 if linked with customer SLA degradation

- Alert: Unexpected token reuse drop
  - Query: capacity_reuse_rate < 10% vs baseline for 15m
  - Severity: P2

Suggested dashboard panels (example table)

| Metric | Description | Owner | Alert Threshold |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| capacity_reuse_rate | % of burst tokens served by reused capacity | Allocator team | < 10% (P2) |
| coalesced_p99 | P99 latency for coalesced shards | Runtime team | > 1.07x baseline (P1) |
| eviction_count | number of forced tenant evictions | Operator team | > 50/min (P0) |

Runbook: Hotset misbehavior (operator playbook)

Trigger conditions:
- Hotset P99 regression alert OR Eviction storm alert.

Immediate actions (operator)
1) Pause coalescing: set allocator flag region.hotset.enabled=false for the affected region.
2) Revert last placement change if one exists: allocator revert --id <last-deploy-id> --region <region>.
3) Check competing signals:
   - Are there spike in seq_len or model changes? (query heatmap: /api/heatmap?region=R)
   - Any upstream model rollout ids in last 30 minutes? Check /deployments service.
4) If P99 doesn't recover in 10 minutes, trigger tenant-level backfills: mark top 10 coalesced tenants for dedicated warmset (operator UI).
5) Notify incident channel (#platform-hotset) and assign SRE on-call.

Post-incident steps:
- Run the incident checklist and generate a retrospective within 5 business days.
- Capture root cause and update the simulator with the new workload pattern.

Canary and rollout gating policy

- Canary phases: 5% (48h) -> 20% (72h) -> 50% (7d) -> Full (gradual).
- Gating checks every phase:
  - P99 delta <= +3%
  - Eviction rate <= 20% above baseline
  - Operator manual approval after 20% phase

Testing & simulation

- Use the simulator harness (prefetch-sim v3) against real heatmaps. Required tests:
  - Worst-case burst coalescing with 95th percentile seq_len distribution.
  - Model mix shift test (large model to small model transitions).
  - Failure injection: simulated node OOM and preemption.

Ownership and teams

- Allocator team: implement placement policy and flags (owner: Diego Alvarez).
- Runtime team: KV cache co-ordination and metrics (owner: Mei Chen).
- Observability: dashboard and alert ownership (owner: Platform Analytics — Sriram Iyer).
- Operators: runbook execution and UI (owner: Platform Ops — Clara Ortiz).

Risk register (summary)

- Risk: unexpected multi-tenant interference raising tail latency. Mitigation: strict canaries, conservative thresholds, per-tenant opt-out.
- Risk: billing disputes from tenants seeing increased throttles. Mitigation: documentation and per-tenant annotation for coalesced placement.
- Risk: increased complexity for on-call operators. Mitigation: invest in automation for rollback and clear UIs.

Open questions and required decisions

- Decide final hotness score formula weights (simulation results due Q1 2026).
- Decide cross-region eligibility rules for coalescing customers with different data residency needs.

Acceptance criteria (for GA)

- Technical: capacity_reuse_rate >= 20% sustained for 30 days in at least two regions.
- SLO: p99 impact <= +5% and no P0 incidents attributable to coalescing in 90 days.
- Operational: one consolidated operator runbook and dashboard with playbook links published.

Retrospective plan

- After Q4 2026 rollups, run a 3–4 week retro focusing on: simulator fidelity, operator cognitive load, and customer impact. Deliverables: action items tracked in Jira, updated runbook, and ticket for tariff/repricing if savings exceed 25%.

Appendix: useful commands and queries

- Pause hotset in region: curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/allocator/flags -d '{"region":"us-west-2","hotset_enabled":false}'
- Query heatmap: GET /api/telemetry/heatmap?region=us-west-2&window=1h
- Revert allocator deploy: allocatorctl revert --deploy-id d-20260302 --region us-west-2

Related documentation

- See: Heatset affinity spec (link above), Predictive scale runbook, Operator UI styleguide.
